chapter.title: Battle for Detroit
chapter.note: Rebuilt on 6 November 2026 from the six PowerPyx 100% charts (Kara Leaving Detroit, Kara Captured, Connor’s Last Mission, Connor at the CyberLife Tower, Markus Demonstration, Markus Revolution; about 544 nodes, 61 endings) and the game’s text (templates 32.1 to 32.6, the press-dirty-bomb component and the endings page, resolved against the string table). Played in blocks: the President’s press conference → Connor (rooftop for a machine, tower for a deviant) → Kara Leaving Detroit → Markus (demonstration, revolution, or North leading) → Kara Captured (it reads the revolution’s outcome) → the finale (Connor on stage or in the crowd, Amanda’s garden, Connor as the last leader, the broadcasts) and the credits scenes; then the hostess’s YES / NO (chapter 33). Every template prompt is offered with the game’s labels (the cut scared-android round is not built); free-roam brackets are repeatable scenes; timers are action budgets (the 20-minute bus, the detour’s 11 minutes, the four-minute boat, Alice’s stress, the elevator before floor 31, the revolution’s probability of success); quick-time checks are hidden rolls only where the chart branches (values unsourced). Every ending card is recorded as printed. The wiki states no probability for the chapter. Researched in docs/research/chapters/ch32-battle-for-detroit.md; recap in docs/chapters/ch32-battle-for-detroit-chapter-recap.html.

decisions.title: In the Zen Garden and the Hart Plaza rooftop (Connor’s Last Mission)
decisions.context: A machine Connor takes up a sniper position above Hart Plaza to eliminate the deviant leader. After Markus shot the deviant Connor in Night of the Soul, Amanda first briefs the replacement in the Zen Garden.

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: IN THE ZEN GARDEN / TALK TO AMANDA (only after Markus shot the deviant Connor), then HART PLAZA ROOFTOP, FIND VANTAGE POINT, PREPARE TO SHOOT.

decisions.gate: Connor is a machine (never deviant, or replaced after dying a deviant).
decisions.note: The Zen Garden talk has no lines in the template; it is narrated from the wiki’s Amanda page.

benchmark.note: Two events; the Zen Garden one is gated on Markus shooting the deviant Connor (fallback: the old Night of the Soul choice).

decisions.title: Talk to Hank on the rooftop
decisions.context: Hank follows Connor onto the roof: “Deviant’s blood may be a different color than mine, but they’re alive.” Two dialogue rounds: FRIENDLY / AGGRESSIVE / REASONABLE / THREATENING / STAY QUIET, then THREATEN / PLEAD / DEFY / HANK’S SON, with HANK’S SON (INSIST) once his son was mentioned.

options.label: Any first-round line
options.effect: Flavour; Hank: “Step away from the ledge!”

options.label: HANK’S SON, then HANK’S SON (INSIST)
options.effect: Hank: “Cole died because a human surgeon was too high on red ice to operate!” (with “Everytime you died and came back… I thought about Cole” after two or more deaths). Not insisting costs a large Hank drop.

decisions.gate: Hank alive (did not resign and kill himself). Hank large down on arrival (wiki).
decisions.note: The wiki gates HANK’S SON on the Russian Roulette photo; the template has no lock, so it is always offered.

benchmark.note: An event for Hank’s arrival (Hank −2) and three prompts in the game’s order.

decisions.title: Give up the assassination or fight Hank?
decisions.context: Hank stands between Connor and the rifle. The template’s last rooftop prompt: LEAVE (locked “Be friend with Hank”) / ATTACK.

options.label: LEAVE
options.effect: CONNOR LEFT ROOFTOP; Hank lives. Hank −2 if Connor never insisted about his son.

options.label: ATTACK
options.effect: A fight: CONNOR WINS (Hank hangs from the edge) or HANK WINS (“Just a machine.”, CYBERLIFE DECIDED TO SEND ANOTHER CONNOR). Hank −2.

decisions.gate: Machine route; Hank alive. LEAVE needs Hank a Friend when he arrives (before the arrival drop). If Hank died, Captain Allen confronts Connor instead.
decisions.note: The wiki adds “if Connor asked twice about Hank’s son” to LEAVE; the template’s lock (Friend) wins.

benchmark.note: LEAVE / ATTACK with a fight roll on ATTACK (benchmark value 0.25).

decisions.title: Save Hank after the rooftop fight?
decisions.context: Hank hangs from the roof: “Moment of truth, Connor… What are you gonna do?” SAVE HANK / KILL HANK.

options.label: SAVE HANK
options.effect: Hank rushes Connor: DODGE ATTACK (Hank falls to his death) or FAIL TO DODGE ATTACK (Connor falls and is destroyed; another Connor is sent).

options.label: KILL HANK
options.effect: Connor lets go; Hank dies. MISSED OPPORTUNITY, CONNOR LEFT ROOFTOP.

decisions.gate: Machine Connor wins the rooftop fight against Hank.

benchmark.note: The dodge is a roll on SAVE HANK (benchmark value 0.15); the old scene never let Connor die here.

decisions.title: Captain Allen on the rooftop
decisions.context: With Hank dead, Captain Allen’s team finds Connor: “Put the rifle down…” OBEY / EXPLAIN / CONTINUE, then FIGHT / FLEE.

options.label: FIGHT
options.effect: KILL ALLEN AND HIS MEN (MISSED OPPORTUNITY, CONNOR LEFT ROOFTOP) or ALLEN DESTROYS CONNOR (another Connor is sent).

options.label: FLEE
options.effect: CONNOR JUMPS OFF THE ROOF: a death; another Connor is sent.

decisions.gate: Machine route; Hank committed suicide in Night of the Soul.
decisions.note: Allen’s greeting depends on whether Connor died in The Hostage. FLEE is not a peaceful exit (the old scene called it one).

benchmark.note: The talk round, then FIGHT (roll 0.35, benchmark value) / FLEE.

decisions.title: The tower elevator
decisions.context: A deviant Connor walks into CyberLife Tower as the machine they sent and is escorted into the elevator to level 31. Free roam FIND A WAY TO ESCAPE before the elevator reaches level 31: spot and hack the camera, try the panel, attack the guards, then hack the elevator with AGENT 54 VOICE or CONNOR’S VOICE.

options.label: AGENT 54 VOICE after neutralizing the guards
options.effect: REDIRECT ELEVATOR to floor -49.

options.label: CONNOR’S VOICE
options.effect: Rejected: “Voice of RK800 model recognized. You are not authorized…”

options.label: Lose the guard fight
options.effect: CONNOR WAS SHOT BY SECURITY.

options.label: Run out of time
options.effect: AMANDA WARNS CONNOR, CONNOR WAS AMBUSHED AND SHOT.

decisions.gate: Deviant Connor alive (Markus spared him).
decisions.note: The timer is an action budget (six floors per action, benchmark value): the full route plus one wasted action fits.

benchmark.note: The lobby TV, an arrival event and one repeatable elevator scene.

decisions.title: Floor -49
decisions.context: The elevator opens on the warehouse. With the camera hacked Connor walks out; otherwise guards are waiting (ELIMINATE GUARDS or CONNOR WAS SHOT BY SECURITY). Connor starts converting the androids.

options.label: Camera hacked
options.effect: LEAVE ELEVATOR.

options.label: Camera functional
options.effect: A fight with no alternative.

decisions.gate: Connor redirected the elevator.

benchmark.note: Two variants and the conversion event (the other Connor holds Hank hostage, or shoots Connor when Hank is dead).

decisions.title: The other Connor holds Hank hostage
decisions.context: Connor-60: “Him… Or the revolution.” GUARANTEE / HANK / BLUFF / CONVINCE, then the choice.

options.label: Any line
options.effect: Flavour; Connor-60: “Enough talk!”

decisions.gate: Hank alive.

benchmark.note: One prompt in the game’s order.

decisions.title: Save Hank or continue the conversion?
decisions.context: A duplicate Connor holds Hank hostage on floor -49: SAVE HANK / SACRIFICE HANK.

options.label: SAVE HANK
options.effect: Hank +2. Then SHOOT / INTERPOSE / CONVERT / TIMEOUT.

options.label: SACRIFICE HANK
options.effect: Hank −2; Connor-60 shoots Hank and damages Connor; the conversion finishes or not (roll), then the four-way choice.

decisions.gate: Deviant Connor reaches the warehouse; Hank alive.

benchmark.note: The conversion after the sacrifice is a roll (benchmark value 0.25).

decisions.title: Saving Hank: shoot, interpose, convert, or nothing
decisions.context: After giving in: SHOOT / INTERPOSE lead to the Connors’ fight (win outright → THE ANDROIDS WOKE UP with Hank alive; draw → Hank’s questions); CONVERT is the sacrifice by another route; TIMEOUT is OUT OF TIME → THE ANDROIDS REMAINED DORMANT.

options.label: SHOOT / INTERPOSE
options.effect: CONNORS FIGHT: a roll; a draw leads to Hank’s questions.

options.label: CONVERT
options.effect: Hank is killed; the conversion finishes; the four-way choice.

options.label: TIMEOUT
options.effect: Hank injured, Connor killed, androids dormant.

decisions.gate: Connor chose SAVE HANK.
decisions.note: CONVERT has no chart node of its own (research §8 item 12); the template says it leads to the same result as sacrificing Hank and converting.

benchmark.note: Fight roll 0.3 (benchmark value) on SHOOT and INTERPOSE.

decisions.title: Prove which Connor Hank should trust
decisions.context: Hank holds both Connors at gunpoint and asks two questions: his dog (SUMO / SCOUT / JACK / BUDDY; a wrong answer changes nothing) and his son (COLE / ANTHONY / GABRIEL / ELLIOTT).

options.label: COLE
options.effect: Hank +2 and shoots the other Connor; RESUME CONVERSION; THE ANDROIDS WOKE UP with Hank alive.

options.label: A wrong name
options.effect: Hank shoots the real Connor; THE ANDROIDS REMAINED DORMANT.

decisions.gate: The Connors’ fight ended in a draw.
decisions.note: Knowledge test, not a moral choice; COLE is always offered and is marked as remembered when Connor saw the photo in Russian Roulette.

benchmark.note: Two prompts in the game’s order (the old scene asked one combined question).

decisions.title: Any last words? (the damaged Connor)
decisions.context: Connor-60 stands over the damaged Connor: STAND UP / SHOOT / TRANSFER / TIMEOUT. TRANSFER swaps bodies and the androids wake; otherwise Connor dies, with the androids awake only if the conversion had finished.

options.label: TRANSFER
options.effect: THE ANDROIDS WOKE UP; Connor survives in the other body; a shot Hank dies in his arms.

options.label: STAND UP / SHOOT / TIMEOUT
options.effect: Connor dies: THE ANDROIDS WOKE UP (conversion finished) or THE ANDROIDS REMAINED DORMANT.

decisions.gate: After SACRIFICE HANK, CONVERT, or the other Connor’s shot when Hank is dead.

benchmark.note: One prompt; the outcome depends on whether the conversion finished.

decisions.title: A Detroit street: the last bus in 20 minutes
decisions.context: Start variants: Luther with Kara (Jericho never attacked), Luther a captive (saved in Crossroads), or Luther dead. Optional looks (SEE HANGED ANDROID, WATCH BROADCAST ABOUT JERICHO’S ATTACK) and, without Luther, Alice is cold: DEACTIVATE / LEAVE ON. Then FIND A GUN or LUTHER FINDS A GUN, HIDE FROM MILITARY, SNEAK PAST SOLDIERS.

options.label: Look around / talk to Alice
options.effect: Each costs a minute of the 20-minute bus timer.

options.label: Sneak past the soldiers
options.effect: SPOTTED BY SOLDIERS on failure: arrested, Kara Captured.

decisions.gate: Kara escaped Crossroads (not captured).
decisions.note: The broadcast exists only after the Jericho raid.

benchmark.note: A start event, a repeatable street scene with a minute budget, the gun and hiding event, and the risky sneak.

decisions.title: Save the Jerrys or Luther, or keep going?
decisions.context: Soldiers are loading captured androids into a truck: two Jerrys, or Luther and a Jerry.

options.label: SAVE THE JERRYS / SAVE LUTHER
options.effect: Alice small up. Success: GRAB ROCK, HIT SOLDIER WITH ROCK, the Jerrys flee or Luther joins. Fail: SPOTTED BY SOLDIERS, arrested.

options.label: KEEP GOING
options.effect: Alice small down; a captive Luther is left behind.

decisions.gate: Kara on the Leaving route.

benchmark.note: Template labels and arrows; the save is a risky action (unsourced 0.2). No Luther arrow and no roadside execution.

decisions.title: Checkpoint or detour?
decisions.context: The route HUD: CHECKPOINT: RISKY 0.750KM - 3MIN; DETOUR: SAFER 1.7KM - 11MIN.

options.label: APPROACH CHECKPOINT
options.effect: Three minutes; the soldier’s questions and the glove. No capture.

options.label: TAKE DETOUR
options.effect: Eleven minutes: on time with 11 or more left, otherwise LATE FOR THE BUS (Alice and Luther small down).

decisions.gate: Kara reached the checkpoint.

benchmark.note: No roll: the old capture risk is gone; lateness follows the minute budget.

decisions.title: Checkpoint questions
decisions.context: Soldier: “Where are you going?” (ALICE EXCUSE with Luther / CURFEW / CAR BROKEDOWN / BUS); with Luther, STAY CALM / STAY ATTENTIVE; “She’s trembling” (SICK / COLD with Luther / FEAR).

options.label: Any answer
options.effect: No effect; the soldier lets them go and calls after them.

decisions.gate: Kara approached the checkpoint.

benchmark.note: Three template prompts, with the template’s Luther-only options.

decisions.title: Shoot when the guard calls back?

options.label: SHOOT

options.label: DO NOTHING

decisions.gate: Kara approached the checkpoint.

benchmark.note: Template labels; the Luther second round is its own scene.

decisions.title: Keep a family’s bus tickets?

options.effect: Alice small up, Luther small down (wiki); the terminal stays open.

options.label: KEEP TICKETS
options.effect: Asked again; a second KEEP: Alice small down, Luther small up, BOARD THE BUS (REASSURE / HONEST on the bus).

decisions.gate: Kara on time at the terminal.

benchmark.note: Two rounds as in the template; the second RETURN carries no arrow.

options.effect: DIVERSION LUTHER (river, Luther lost) / PAPERS / FLEE (SOLDIERS EXECUTED KARA[, ALICE & LUTHER]).

options.label: Any

decisions.title: President Warren’s press conference: which questions?
decisions.context: Nov 10, 9:24 PM: Warren declares a national curfew and orders all androids handed over to camps; the journalists shout questions.

options.label: HACKING / DEVIANT LEADER / WORRYING THEFT / CYBERLIFE / INTELLIGENT LIFE / DEVIANTS / RECALL CENTERS / JERICHO ASSAULT / ARMY / PUBLIC OPINION
options.effect: Warren answers the chosen question; nothing changes.

decisions.gate: Chapter start, every path; JERICHO ASSAULT only if Jericho was raided; DEVIANT LEADER and PUBLIC OPINION have two variants.
decisions.note: Off-chart (template 32.5 “President Warren talks to journalists”). The wiki: “up to 4 or 5” questions.

benchmark.note: A Player event for the statement, then a repeatable scene of the ten questions; four are answered (the benchmark’s pick between the wiki’s 4 and 5). “Positive” opinion read as Sympathetic or better. No stat change.

decisions.note: Chart: HART PLAZA FREEDOM MARCH, LEAD JERICHO, ROADBLOCK, TALK TO OFFICER, ANDROIDS UNDER FIRE.
